messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: Computer-assisted nonlinear optimization with interval-arithmetic verification

Propose ONE conjecture in response, within that direction.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>"}

message.content: {"conjecture": "The optimal configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the maximum minimum triangle area is uniquely realized (up to the square's symmetry group) by a specific point set computable via a two-phase procedure: first, nonlinear optimization using a smoothed min-area objective with multistart initializations from perturbed lattice arrangements to escape local maxima, and second, rigorous verification of global optimality using interval arithmetic branch-and-bound that prunes all configurations whose minimum triangle area falls below the computed candidate value. The conjectured optimal minimum triangle area is approximately 1/72, achieved by a configuration related to a perturbed 3×4 triangular lattice with an inserted interior point positioned at the area-centroid of its nearest-neighbor triangle. The interval-arithmetic verification succeeds because the Hessian of the minimum-area functional is sufficiently well-conditioned near the optimum, allowing tight enclosure of all critical points within bounding boxes of diameter O(1/100)."}
